memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Jacob lived in Egypt seventeen years, and the years of his life were a hundred and forty-seven." — Gen 47:28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Seventeen years. Read that number carefully, because it appears once before in this story. Joseph was seventeen when his brothers sold him (Gen 37:2).

Seventeen years of Joseph's life with his father before they were torn apart. And now seventeen years given back, at the end of Jacob's life, in Egypt.

Scripture does not draw attention to it. But it is there, quietly, for anyone reading slowly — a small sign that God had not forgotten what was taken. He gave back the years.

Centuries later God would say through Joel that He would repay the years the locusts had eaten (Joel 2:25). That promise was spoken to Israel in a particular situation, and we should not turn it into a guarantee that God will restore every specific loss in this life. Many losses are not returned to us here.

But God's character is unchanging, and this is what He is like. He is a restorer. What He does not give back in this life, He more than answers in the next, where He wipes away every tear and makes all things new (Rev 21:4-5).

Jacob got seventeen years back. We are promised something better still.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What years or losses do you still grieve?
2. How does God's character as a restorer comfort you?
3. Where might God already have given back more than you noticed?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You see everything that has been taken from me. Thank You that You are a God who restores, and that whatever is not returned in this life is answered fully in the life to come. Amen.
